hearthstead.guide.attributes.body: Every settler has eight numeric attributes, each shown from 0 to 100: Strength for heavy work and carrying; Stamina for keeping pace while tired; Wits for learning; Dexterity for precise hands; Spirit for morale under pressure; Perception for finding targets; Focus for staying on task; and Presence for leading and reassuring others. Newcomers begin low, except for one natural knack that leans higher. The numbers make people different; they never choose the worker for you.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.body2: Attributes grow only by doing the work that trains them — a lumberer's axe builds Strength, a courier's rounds build Stamina. Growth is slow and never finishes: a settler trained for weeks is one you built. Wits speeds every attribute's growth, itself included, so schooling a clever settler early pays for life. Most settlers carry a trait, sometimes two, and every trait costs something: strong backs carry more and walk slower; quick studies learn faster, a step behind on everything else.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.title: Attributes
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.body: Workers have Energy and a visible Work Pace, not a hidden daily-work quota. As Energy falls, they keep accepting valid work but move and complete it more slowly. They do not abruptly stop for the rest of the day because an invisible allowance reached zero. Check the settler sheet to see both Energy and the current pace.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.body2: Rest and the normal daily routine restore Energy. Stamina determines how much pace a tired worker keeps: stronger Stamina means a higher minimum pace when Energy is low. A tired worker may be much slower, but a valid task remains valid; equipment, route and workplace blockers are reported separately.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.title: Work Pace
hearthstead.guide.day.body:
The whole settlement shares one clock. At Rise everyone wakes and the square fills; through Morning and Afternoon Work they walk to their trade — unless it is farmed or felled, where the work already is. At the midday Meal they gather in the dining hall, and come Evening the tavern and square fill again before Rest sends everyone to bed. A phase is a habit, never a law: a raid or real exhaustion overrides it. Guards keep half their number on a night watch, so someone is always walking.

TAVERN TABLES
Hire an Innkeeper by buying their Job Emblem from the Mayor, holding it and right-clicking the intended settler. Keep ready-to-eat food and at least one glass bottle together in one chest or barrel inside the Tavern; the bottle is reusable. Wheat is an ingredient: craft vanilla bread before it becomes a meal. Edible carrots and beetroots can feed the Hearth when a Courier carries them from linked Warehouse storage; a Tavern needs ready food and reusable bottles in its own service store. Keep spare meals and glass bottles in linked Warehouse storage. A Courier refills a staffed Tavern after the Hearth has its food reserve. Place an Another Furniture wooden chair facing an adjacent wooden table. Keep the chair pulled out. You can also use a bottom-half straight stair with its low side facing a fence topped by a wooden pressure plate. Leave a clear side aisle beside the chair and space across the table for the host to stand. Keep the furniture and both approach spaces inside the linked Tavern. Residents visit during Meal and Evening when free from work and urgent needs. Guards keep their watch and orders.
hearthstead.guide.day.title: The Day
hearthstead.guide.founding.body:
Craft a Hearth from logs, stone and a campfire, then place it on open ground away from another settlement. Three available settlers and a dedicated Mayor found your village. Keep prepared food in the Hearth and give your workers safe homes and clear walking routes.

FIRST WORKER
Bring local logs to the visiting merchant and open their trade window. Ordinary player-gathered logs are Basic quality and can earn Coins immediately. The first four Basic log sales cost 34 logs in total and pay 4 Coins. Offers have limited uses and repeated sales raise the requested quantity.

Open Hearth → Tech Tree and learn Timber Rights for 2 Coins. Craft and register a Lumber Camp, then buy a Lumberer Emblem from the Mayor for 2 Coins. Use it on an available settler. Supply a serviceable iron axe and mark natural trees with the Work Scepter. The worker's first stored logs make Stores and Roads available.

Coins are physical items. Purchases use your inventory, then the bound Hearth, then valid linked Warehouse storage. The displayed cost and refusal explain what is missing.
hearthstead.guide.founding.title: Founding
hearthstead.guide.jobs.body: Jobs are authorised by physical Job Emblems. Learn and register the workplace, then buy its Emblem from the living Mayor. Hold it in your main hand and right-click a compatible settler without sneaking: Hearthstead consumes it once and automatically assigns the nearest valid workplace. There is no separate Hire button. Every new worker starts with no job equipment; their need icon, inventory and Hearth → Tasks show the real item they need. Rejected assignments do not consume the Emblem. Empty both hands and Shift-right-click a settler when you want to open their inventory yourself.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.title: Jobs
hearthstead.guide.logistics.body:
Workers collect and deliver physical goods using their bags and workplace storage. Open Hearth → Tasks to inspect a delivery's goods, source-to-target route, assigned Courier, physical owner and Stop reason. Real stacks move from the workplace chest through the Courier bag into Warehouse storage. Equipment follows a real request from storage to the worker. A blocked route or missing tool stays visible until its cause is resolved.

Open Hearth → Stores to find goods and inspect the loaded Warehouse locations that hold them. This is a stock overview; open the real chest to take items. An unloaded Warehouse is not reported as an empty one.

Worker-made goods can have better quality than ordinary goods. Basic logs start at 8 per Coin; Fine, Superior and Exceptional logs start at 4, 3 and 2. Each offer has finite stock, and repeated sales can raise the shipment size. Moving goods through a bag or chest does not improve quality. Check the exact offer before trading.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.title: Logistics
hearthstead.guide.mayor.body: Your dedicated Mayor arrives with the three founding workers. The Mayor cannot take another job, and their knack decides what it grows good at — a strong mayor quickens every trade, a clever one speeds learning, a warm one steadies morale, and so for all eight attributes. A new mayor's gift takes a day and a half to show, so swapping ahead of a raid you can see coming works, but swapping every morning does not. Losing a mayor is a real blow: morale falls settlement-wide. A successor can take the vacant seat, but their boon remains unavailable while the settlement mourns for three days.
hearthstead.guide.mayor.title: The Mayor
hearthstead.guide.plaque.body: A hung plaque starts blank and does nothing at all — no screen, no scan — until you fit a Build Plan into it. Craft a plan for the building you want and use it on the plaque: that stamps its purpose and sets it surveying the room around it. The plaque glows what it finds: dark while blank, red until something is met, amber once part of the room qualifies, green the moment all of it does.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.body2:
Each building has its own requirements for floor space, furniture, storage and access. Right-click its plaque for the exact checklist. Green checks show fulfilled requirements; missing entries explain what to build. The room is checked again automatically; Refresh requests a new reading.

After Timber Rights, craft a Work Scepter from 2 flint, 1 copper ingot and 2 sticks. Hold it and right-click a Lumber Camp, Farmhouse or the employed worker. Right-click each corner, then right-click the height. Review and confirm the outlined work area. Trees and crops must be inside that area.

A building may be placed beyond the Hearth's central area when it is linked to the settlement. Keep entrances and routes usable. Valid beds are yellow when free and green when assigned.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.title: The Plaque
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.body:
Travelers qualify during ordinary play while the settlement has a bound Hearth, a valid Tavern, available housing, sufficient morale and a food reserve. A waiting guest keeps the exact price shown on their card. New guests ask for Coins: starting aptitude sets the premium and the applicable discount is fixed when that guest appears. Older guests may keep an existing bread-and-planks quote. You can earn Coins while the guest waits. Read the exact card price before recruiting; it is charged only on successful recruitment.

Recruitment still needs a free bed and eight ready meals per resident after the newcomer joins. Coin payment can use your inventory, the bound Hearth and valid linked Warehouse containers. A retained barter quote uses its original payment rules. Admission charges only when the required checks succeed.

A waiting traveler may sit in a staffed Tavern. Visiting guests with Coins pay one Coin when they receive a meal; payment goes into available settlement storage. Residents use the normal meal service. Sitting and buying a meal do not make a visitor a resident, and recruiting never bypasses the bed check.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.title: Recruiting
hearthstead.guide.research.body: Research needs a built and registered Architect's Study. First complete the first-raid aftermath, then learn Hearth Doctrine in Development at the Hearth: keep every resident housed for 20 continuous minutes, physically fulfil 5 equipment requests, and pay 6 Coins. The first doctrine learned remains the settlement's primary tradition, while the other released doctrines can still be earned later at full quest and material cost. Build the study with its learned plan, then right-click its lectern to open the research bench. Hire a scholar to advance projects. An employed scholar also adds a little daily progress when not actively working at the lectern. Each project costs paper and a trade sample. Cancelling returns half the sample, never the paper.
hearthstead.guide.research.body2: The catalogue lists six projects. Crop Rotation, Guard Training and Seasoned Timber can currently be started. Better Yeast, Bellows Smelting and Tannic Acid remain listed for saved progress, but new starts wait for their bakery, smelter and tannery trades to be released. Seasoned timber may be researched before unlocking or building a sawmill; its bonus helps only when a sawyer produces there. Choose one project at a time and pay its displayed physical cost. Completed research gives a permanent bonus. Existing paid projects can still progress or be cancelled. Research is optional.
hearthstead.guide.research.title: Research
hearthstead.guide.saga.body: Every raid captain who reaches your walls has a name, and one who gets away with what they came for earns a second — 'the Grain-Thief' for one who stole your harvest, 'Larder's Bane' for one who has done it more than once — each a claim you can check against the raid's own report. A captain remembers too: the settler who hurt them most becomes a grudge carried into the next fight, and cutting one down only passes it on — whoever answers next inherits both the grudge and a name sworn to the one who fell.
hearthstead.guide.saga.title: The Saga
hearthstead.guide.summons.body: Right-click a working building's plaque and press Summon to call whoever works there straight to their post — useful for a farmer sleeping off a bad night in the wrong field, or a guard who wandered off to watch instead of fight. A bell rings where you stood; the settler answers with a low murmur wherever they are, then starts walking, glowing the whole way through walls so you can watch them coming. A summons lasts about a minute and a half — past that they simply forget they were called, and the glow fades with it.
hearthstead.guide.summons.title: Summons
hearthstead.guide.threat.body: Prepare for the first raid through Journey at the Hearth. Build your settlement, house its residents, and equip both a Guard and an Archer with real weapons, arrows and orders. Choose Check Readiness to see what is still missing. Once every check passes, choose Declare Ready to schedule the first attack. A warning will announce its date, direction and objective before the raiders arrive.
hearthstead.guide.threat.body2: After the raid, open Journey at the Hearth to review the Aftermath and the road ahead. Check the recorded outcome and losses, replace missing equipment, and restore food reserves before expanding again. The first declaration is a preparation milestone, not a permanent shield: later raids follow the settlement's threat and raid rules, so keep defenders supplied and ready.
hearthstead.guide.threat.title: Threat
hearthstead.guide.title: Settler's Handbook
hearthstead.guide.watch.body: A newly assigned Guard starts without a weapon or armour. Their need icon opens a real equipment request: place a serviceable weapon in Warehouse storage and a Courier carries it through their bag to the Barracks and Guard. Open Guard Orders from the settler sheet to choose Hold Here, Defend Hearth, a two-to-eight-point Patrol, or Clear. After Arm the Watch, an Archer assigned to a linked Watchtower can receive the separate Tower Post command. Neither defender can fight properly until the requested physical weapon arrives.
hearthstead.guide.watch.body2: Rank is earned through patrols and real combat, never selected. Each credited hostile kill grants combat XP once and plays the experience cue. Strength unlocks the Guard's later abilities; any rank armour must also exist in settlement storage before it can be worn, so promotion never conjures equipment. The highest-ranked living defender becomes the settlement's captain. Archers follow the same physical-equipment rule for bows and arrows, earn their own combat progress, and return to their persisted patrol or tower order after a fight.
hearthstead.guide.watch.title: The Watch

journey.hearthstead.step.fj_250_courier_: Wait for one Courier to reserve the request and its exact physical stacks.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_260_warehous: The Courier must pick up, carry and deposit the reserved logs into Warehouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_300_unlock_f: Pay the Development cost for Cultivated Ground to learn the Farmhouse plan.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_310_link_far: Build and link a valid Farmhouse with accessible workplace storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_320_staff_fa: Buy a Farmer Emblem, hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler with a compatible Farmhouse post without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_330_set_farm: Use the Work Scepter to confirm a bounded zone containing farmland or planted crops.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_340_farmer_r: Let the Farmer assess the field and publish the exact physical hoe requirement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_350_equip_fa: Move a compatible physical hoe into the Farmer's inventory or Farmhouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_360_supply_f: Place an accepted physical seed in linked Farmhouse storage; the Farmer must withdraw and plant that exact seed inside the confirmed field.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_370_farmhous: The Farmer must harvest a mature crop and place the conserved output in Farmhouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_380_warehous: A Courier must complete the physical crop pickup and deposit it in Warehouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_400_unlock_h: Unlock the Home node to learn the House and Lodging build plans.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_410_link_fir: Build and link a valid House or Lodging so the settlement gains real resident capacity.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_420_unlock_t: Pay the Development cost for Hospitality to learn the Tavern plan.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_430_link_tav: Build and link a valid Tavern before inviting travelers.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_440_recruitm: Meet the live housing, food, safety, morale and Tavern requirements for a recruitment cycle.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_450_traveler: Keep the Tavern valid until the chosen traveler physically arrives and waits for a decision.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_460_admit_tr: Meet the traveler at the Tavern and recruit them into your settlement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_500_unlock_f: After a real Courier delivery, pay the Development cost for the First Watch to learn the Barracks plan and Guard Emblem. A founder may take the Guard post; the Mayor remains dedicated.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_510_link_bar: Build and link a valid Barracks with accessible storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_520_staff_ba: Buy a Guard Emblem, hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler with a compatible Barracks post without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_530_guard_re: Let the Guard assess duty and publish the exact compatible physical weapon requirement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_540_equip_gu: Move one compatible physical weapon into the Guard's inventory or Barracks storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_550_set_guar: Commit a valid Stand Post or Patrol Route assignment for the equipped Guard.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_551_unlock_a: Research Arm the Watch at the Hearth to learn the Watchtower plan and unlock the Archer Emblem and Tower Post command.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_552_add_fift: Keep at least five unique physical bed heads inside valid linked Houses or Lodgings before calling another traveler.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_553_second_r: Keep the Tavern, five beds, food reserve, morale and joining price ready. The next natural attempt, and every retry until this Watch recruit is admitted, qualifies in four to eight minutes.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_554_second_t: Keep the exact linked Tavern valid until this Watch slot's natural traveler physically arrives and waits for your decision.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_555_admit_fi: Recruit the waiting traveler to welcome a fifth member to your settlement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_556_link_wat: Build and link a valid Watchtower with an accessible physical storage container for arrows.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_557_staff_wa: Buy an Archer Emblem, hold it in your main hand and right-click a current settler beside the compatible linked Watchtower without sneaking. The Archer must be a different settler from the Guard.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_558_archer_r: Let the Archer assess the tower and publish the exact serviceable physical bow requirement in the request queue.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559_equip_ar: Supply a serviceable physical bow and let a Courier complete the real request into the Archer's main hand.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559a_supply_: Place at least eight physical Arrows in storage inside this linked Watchtower, then confirm the next Tower Post command; that command verifies the exact rack and advances both facts together.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559b_set_tow: Open Guard Orders for the equipped Archer and choose Tower Post. The commit must point to this linked Watchtower and re-observe its physical arrows.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_560_declare_: With five live settlers, five physical beds, one armed ordered Guard and one bow-and-arrow Tower Post Archer, choose Check Readiness and Declare Ready.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_600_receive_: The persisted raid plan will announce its date, direction and objective before the attack.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_610_first_ra: Defend the settlement until the server records the real raid outcome and losses.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_620_review_a: Open Journey at the Hearth after the raid to review the persisted report and the road ahead.
